document.title: The taxpayer's own record of rental property income and expenses (Schedule E Part I)
document.issued_by: nobody - the taxpayer's own rental income and expense summary
document.notes: Rents a tenant pays directly are reported by no information return; a property manager's 1099-MISC box 1 covers only what the manager collected. Schedule E Part I's columns A/B/C are three PROPERTIES, so one record describes one property and which column it takes is not part of the address.

extraction.note: A taxpayer's own record. No prescribed layout, so no structured model and no boxes to read: it prints ITEMS in the client's own words, and which declared box each belongs in is a JUDGEMENT a person confirms (spec 075 group D, clarification Q1). Read by the declared custom model in TRANSCRIBE mode - the same reader, a second template - which copies every line verbatim and names no destination. A separate, cheap proposal call then suggests a box per item; **only a box a person confirms places anything**, so an engagement with nineteen rental sheets shows an empty Schedule E until somebody has looked. That is the decision, not a defect.

custom.reads: a client's own record of rental income and expenses, usually one block per property
